extracted.intended_audience: authors submitting to ACL Rolling Review (ARR)
extracted.subtask_description: A pre-submission checklist for authors preparing manuscripts for ARR covering scope, authorship and registration, dual submissions/resubmissions, formatting, anonymization, responsible NLP requirements, and supplemental materials to avoid desk rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: The paper follows the scope of ARR CFP. ARR is a reviewing venue that mainly serves the conferences of the Association for Computational Linguistics, and the submissions are expected to make a contribution to the computational processing of language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the submission makes a clear contribution to computational language processing; consult the ARR call for papers to verify scope before submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author list completeness and finality
rubrics_metrics.description: All authors are included and in the final order. No changes to author list or author order will be allowed after submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the guidelines on authorship criteria and confirm final author list and order with all coauthors prior to submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship criteria awareness
rubrics_metrics.description: Please consult the guidelines on authorship criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make sure all listed authors meet ARR/ACL authorship criteria; resolve disputes before submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: OpenReview profile completion
rubrics_metrics.description: All authors completed the OpenReview profiles prior to submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete profiles in advance; refer to the provided tutorial to avoid missing required profile information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author reviewing requirement and registration
rubrics_metrics.description: All authors are aware of the new reviewing requirement for all authors and will complete the author registration form within 48h of the submission deadline. Non-complying papers may be desk-rejected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate within the author team to ensure timely completion of author registration; senior authors can mentor secondary reviewers. ARR may desk-reject papers if authors do not contribute appropriately to reviewing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awareness of peer-review incentive policy and deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: All authors are aware of the new policy on incentives in peer review. The work by ‘highly irresponsible’ reviewers or chairs may become ineligible for committing or (re-)submission during the next ARR cycle. All assigned (meta-)reviews must be submitted on time and in accordance with ARR reviewing guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check review/metareview due dates; declare personal emergencies via the emergency declaration form. Ensure team members understand consequences for late or missing reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain updated reviewer profile links and interests
rubrics_metrics.description: All authors update their OpenReview profiles with the correct Semantic Scholar, DBLP, and ACL Anthology links, and update their listed papers to reflect their current research interests, to make sure that they receive relevant manuscripts as review assignments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep external links and research interests current to improve review assignment relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: No dual submissions / exclusivity during ARR review
rubrics_metrics.description: The paper is not and will not be under review at any archival venue while it is reviewed at ARR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not submit the same work to multiple archival venues simultaneously; ensure exclusivity during ARR review period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-copy submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Only one copy of this paper is submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate with coauthors to avoid accidental multiple submissions of the same manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality and salami-slicing
rubrics_metrics.description: If there are any concurrent submissions by the same authors on a related topic, check that it follows the originality requirements. Salami-sliced papers are not welcome and may be desk rejected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure concurrent submissions are sufficiently distinct and satisfy originality requirements; avoid incremental slices of the same work presented as separate submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission: sufficiently different or acknowledged
rubrics_metrics.description: If the paper is presented as a new submission, it must be on a sufficiently different topic so that any prior reviews no longer apply. If the paper is a revision, the submission follows the resubmissions policy in the CFP: the previous version must be acknowledged, and you must provide a summary of changes and revisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don't rely on reframing or incremental improvements to claim novelty; explicitly acknowledge prior versions for resubmissions and include a summary of changes. Optionally include a color-coded version highlighting revisions. If prior criticisms still apply, acknowledge as a resubmission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author changes must be justified (without deanonymizing)
rubrics_metrics.description: If there were any changes to the original set of authors, it is described in the submission form in the field ‘Justification for author changes’. Do NOT include this information in the summary of revisions pdf, as this will deanonymize you.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the designated submission-form field to explain author list changes; never place such explanations inside the (potentially public or reviewer-visible) revision summary PDF.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page limits
rubrics_metrics.description: The paper follows page limits (8 for long, 4 for short, not including limitations and ethical considerations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure main paper length complies with the specified limits; limitations and ethical considerations sections do not count toward these limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations section placement and content
rubrics_metrics.description: The paper has a section titled “Limitations” placed as follows: ACL formatting guidelines. This section can only include the discussion of limitations; strictly no new experiments, figures or analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow ACL formatting for the location of the Limitations section; include only discussion of limitations and avoid adding new experimental material there.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical considerations section labeling and length handling
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have an optional ethics section, we recommend that it is titled ‘Ethical considerations’. This will help us more accurately assess the length of the paper, since Ethics sections will not count towards the page limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Label ethics discussion consistently to ensure correct page-count handling; use the recommended title for clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: ACL formatting compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: The paper follows ACL formatting. You are encouraged to use the ACL pubcheck tool to check for common problems. There is an official Overleaf template. Note that this template has a [review] setting that must be on for the submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use pubcheck and the official template (with review mode on) to avoid formatting errors. Be aware of ACLPUB formatting guideline updates (January 2025) regarding font size in figures/tables, placement of limitations and ethical considerations sections, and two-column formatting of appendices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of limitations, ethics, references, and appendices in main PDF
rubrics_metrics.description: The limitations section, the optional ethical considerations section, references, and appendices should be included in the pdf for the paper (not counting towards the page limit), and not be submitted as a separate PDF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine these sections into the single submission PDF rather than uploading separate documents for them.

rubrics_metrics.name: No leftover comments or meta-text
rubrics_metrics.description: There are no comments or any leftover meta-text from prior revisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remove tracked-change artifacts, comments, and other meta-text before submission to avoid deanonymization or unprofessional presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Appendices are in double-column format, with the exception of math-heavy sections where single-column is needed for readability (guidelines updated in April 2025).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Format appendices as two-column unless readability for math necessitates single-column; follow updated guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human-readable primary text (no machine-manipulation)
rubrics_metrics.description: The full text of the submissions should be addressed exclusively to the human readers, and clearly visible to them. Submissions attempting to manipulate machine readers will be desk rejected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid hiding content or formatting tricks intended to influence automated systems; ensure the paper is directly readable by human reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental materials must be truly supplemental
rubrics_metrics.description: Note that any supplemental materials (code, data, appendices) should be truly supplemental; a reader should be able to understand the work from the paper alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely on supplemental material to convey essential results or methodology required to understand the submission; include core contributions in the paper itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymization of submission text
rubrics_metrics.description: The submission must not contain explicit references to the authors’ prior work or otherwise disclose their identity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remove obvious self-references and any text that would reveal authorship; follow ACL anonymization policies when citing prior work (use anonymized phrasing where appropriate).

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymization of supplementary materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Any supplementary materials are also properly anonymized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure code, data, or other supplements do not contain author-identifying metadata, repository links, or other traces of identity.

rubrics_metrics.name: No acknowledgements in submission
rubrics_metrics.description: The acknowledgements section is not included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Omit acknowledgements from the submitted manuscript to preserve anonymization; include them only in camera-ready if allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: No non-anonymous external links
rubrics_metrics.description: There are no links to non-anonymous repositories or services like Dropbox that may track who opened the link.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid including links that reveal identity via access logs or that are tied to personal accounts; use anonymized or static artifacts if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct preprint status selection
rubrics_metrics.description: The “preprint status” field is filled out appropriately. “We do not intend to release” option is binding. If you are not sure whether you will preprint the paper during the review period, please select the “we are considering…” option.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the preprint option carefully; selecting 'do not intend' is binding. If uncertain, use the intermediate option to avoid mis-declaration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsible NLP research checklist completion
rubrics_metrics.description: The responsible NLP research checklist is filled in appropriately. If you are not sure about any field, please look it up in the guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide justifications, section references, and not just 'yes'/'no' answers. Inappropriately filled checklists (e.g., misleading responses, blanket 'yes' answers, or missing section references) can be considered grounds for desk rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generative AI disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: When responding to the generative AI question, please make sure you follow ACL policy on the authorship and the use of generative AI. If you used generative AI in acceptable ways, e.g. coding or writing assistance, please disclose it in either the acknowledgements or the checklist itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose any acceptable use of generative AI per ACL policy, either in the checklist or acknowledgements (if acknowledgements are allowed later); follow the ACL guidance for how to describe AI assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encouraged documentation: data sheets and model cards
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are encouraged to include data sheets and model cards in supplemental material, as appropriate. They are also encouraged to devote a section of their paper to concerns of the ethical impact of their work and to a discussion of its broader impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include data sheets/model cards where relevant; ethical impact discussion may extend into a 5th page (for short papers) or 9th page (for long papers). Use supplements for additional documentation but ensure core content remains in the paper.
